subject: Business
title: Situational Leadership Theory
description: Learn Situational Leadership Theory in one minute.

hook.text: A new hire needs step-by-step instructions. A veteran needs space. Same leader, completely different approaches.

buildup.text: Hersey and Blanchard's model says leaders should adapt their style to the follower's competence and commitment.

discovery.text: Four styles: directing (low skill), coaching (growing skill), supporting (high skill, low will), delegating (both high).

twist.text: Most leaders have a default style they apply to everyone. Effective leaders flex across all four.

climax.text: A leader who micromanages experts drives them away. One who delegates to novices sets them up to fail.

punchline.text: There's no best leadership style. There's only the right one for right now.

quiz.question: What does situational leadership theory recommend?
options: Adapting your style to each team member's competence and commitment
Using one consistent style for fairness

details.summary: Situational leadership, developed by Hersey and Blanchard, argues that no single leadership style works universally. Effective leaders adapt their approach based on the task at hand and the team member's competence and motivation, ranging from directing to coaching to supporting to delegating.
details.whyItMatters: New employees need direction. Experienced professionals need autonomy. Applying the same leadership style to everyone wastes the potential of skilled team members and overwhelms those who need more guidance.
takeaways: Effective leadership style depends on the follower's competence and commitment
Four styles range from directing to coaching to supporting to delegating
Leaders must assess each situation and adapt their approach accordingly

faq.question: What are the four situational leadership styles?
faq.answer: Directing gives specific instructions and close supervision for low-competence situations. Coaching provides direction while building skills through explanation. Supporting facilitates and empowers competent but unmotivated people.

faq.question: How do you assess which leadership style fits a particular situation?
faq.answer: Evaluate the person's competence to perform the specific task and their commitment or motivation level. A senior engineer may need delegation for familiar tasks but directing for an unfamiliar domain. The same person may require different leadership styles for different aspects of their role.
